Girl with a Pearl Earring. Johannes Vermeer's circa 1665 painting depicts an unknown young woman in an exotic turban and luminous pearl earring, turning over her shoulder in a moment of intimate eye contact. The painting's enigmatic subject, masterful handling of light, and melancholic beauty have made it one of the most recognised works of Dutch Golden Age portraiture.

The girl's subject remains unidentified—possibly Vermeer's daughter, a servant, or an imaginative fancy dress composition called a tronie. She wears an exotic yellow turban and a dark dress against a featureless dark background that throws her face into luminous isolation. The pearl earring—almost certainly not a real pearl but rendered to catch light magnificently—catches and reflects light in Vermeer's signature style and has become the painting's most famous feature.

The work is housed in the Mauritshuis museum in The Hague, where it is one of the most visited artworks in the Netherlands. It famously sparked Tracy Chevalier's 1999 novel Girl with a Pearl Earring and a 2003 film adaptation starring Scarlett Johansson. Vermeer's extraordinarily subtle palette and optical realism suggest he may have used a camera obscura to achieve his precise tonality, a technique that demonstrates his unparalleled ability to render light and psychological presence while reflecting the Dutch Golden Age fascination with intimate cabinet paintings.
